1. Indian National Congress — Overview

  • The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
  • It became the most important political organisation of the Indian national movement.
  • It evolved from an organisation of educated political elites into a mass anti-colonial movement during the Gandhian era.
📌 Must-Memorise

Indian National Congress → Founded in 1885

2. Founder Associated with INC

  • Allan Octavian Hume, commonly known as A.O. Hume, played the central organisational role in establishing the Indian National Congress.
  • Hume was a retired British civil servant.
📌 Must-Memorise

INC → A.O. Hume

3. A.O. Hume

  • Hume had served in the Indian Civil Service.
  • He encouraged educated Indians from different provinces to create an all-India political organisation.

  • Mobilise educated Indians.

20. Political Background of INC

  • Several British policies generated discontent before 1885:
  • Vernacular Press Act.
  • Arms Act.
  • Reduction in the age limit for Civil Service examination.
  • Economic hardship.
  • Racial discrimination.

21. Vernacular Press Act

  • Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 during Lord Lytton's administration.
  • It sought to restrict Indian-language newspapers.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vernacular Press Act → 1878 → Lord Lytton

22. Arms Act

  • Arms Act was also enacted in 1878.
  • It imposed restrictions on possession of arms.

23. Delhi Imperial Assemblage

  • Lord Lytton held the Imperial Assemblage at Delhi in 1877 while severe famine affected parts of India.
  • This contributed to criticism of colonial priorities.

24. Ilbert Bill Controversy

  • The Ilbert Bill controversy occurred in 1883.
  • The bill sought to allow senior Indian judges to try European British subjects in certain cases.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ilbert Bill → 1883

25. European Opposition to Ilbert Bill

  • Strong racial opposition from Europeans forced the government to weaken the original proposal.
  • Educated Indians saw the controversy as evidence of racial discrimination.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Ilbert Bill Controversy → Stimulus to Indian Political Unity

  • The first session of the Indian National Congress began on 28 December 1885.
  • It was held at Bombay.
📌 Must-Memorise

First INC Session → Bombay → 1885

  • The first session was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College → First INC Session

  • The first Congress session was originally planned for Poona.

First INC Session → 72 Delegates

31. Early Character of Congress

  • The early Congress consisted mainly of:
  • Lawyers.
  • Journalists.
  • Teachers.
  • Professionals.
  • Educated middle-class political leaders.

32. Early Objectives

  • The early Congress sought to:
  • Promote political unity.
  • Develop national feeling.
  • Present Indian grievances.
  • Demand administrative reform.
  • Create regular contact among political workers.

33. Safety Valve Theory

  • One interpretation claimed that the Congress was encouraged as a "safety valve" through which Indian discontent could be peacefully expressed.
  • Modern historians do not accept this as a complete explanation for the origin of the Congress.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Safety Valve Theory → Historical Interpretation, Not Proven Sole Explanation

Vande Mataram at INC → Calcutta → 1896

49. Early Congress Phase

  • The period roughly from 1885 to 1905 is generally called the Moderate phase.
📌 Must-Memorise

Moderate Phase → 1885–1905

50. Major Moderate Leaders

  • Important Moderates included:
  • Dadabhai Naoroji.
  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
  • Pherozeshah Mehta.
  • Surendranath Banerjea.
  • M.G. Ranade.
  • Dinshaw Wacha.

51. Moderate Methods

  • Moderates relied mainly on:
  • Petitions.
  • Resolutions.
  • Meetings.
  • Speeches.
  • Constitutional agitation.
  • Representations to British authorities.
📌 Memory Line

Moderates → Prayer + Petition + Protest

52. Moderate Faith in British Liberalism

  • Early Moderates believed that British public opinion could be persuaded to support constitutional reform in India.

53. Moderate Political Demands

  • They demanded:
  • Expansion of legislative councils.
  • More elected representation.
  • Greater Indian participation in administration.
  • Civil rights.
  • Fiscal reform.

54. Indianisation of Services

  • Moderates demanded a larger share of higher government posts for Indians.

55. ICS Examination

  • They demanded simultaneous Civil Service examinations in India and Britain.
📌 Must-Memorise

Moderate Demand → Simultaneous ICS Examination

56. Legislative Councils

  • Early Congress repeatedly demanded expansion and reform of legislative councils.

57. Indian Councils Act 1892

  • Indian Councils Act 1892 enlarged legislative councils.
  • It permitted limited indirect representation and discussion of budgets.
📌 Must-Memorise

Indian Councils Act → 1892

58. Limitations of 1892 Act

  • Councils remained weak.
  • Executive government was not responsible to elected representatives.

59. Separation of Judiciary and Executive

  • Moderates demanded separation of executive and judicial functions.

60. Military Expenditure

  • Congress criticised India's heavy military expenditure.
  • It argued that Indian revenues were being used disproportionately for imperial purposes.

61. Land Revenue

  • Congress demanded reduction in excessive land revenue burdens.

62. Economic Nationalism

  • Moderate leaders systematically criticised the economic effects of colonial rule.
  • This was one of their most important contributions.

63. Dadabhai Naoroji

  • Dadabhai Naoroji became famous for explaining the "Drain of Wealth" from India to Britain.
📌 Must-Memorise

Drain Theory → Dadabhai Naoroji

64. Drain of Wealth

  • The Drain Theory argued that Indian resources left the country through mechanisms such as:
  • Salaries of British officials.
  • Pensions.
  • Home Charges.
  • Profits.
  • Interest payments.

65. Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

  • Dadabhai Naoroji published Poverty and Un-British Rule in India in 1901.
📌 Must-Memorise

Poverty and Un-British Rule in India → Dadabhai Naoroji

66. Grand Old Man of India

  • Dadabhai Naoroji is popularly called the Grand Old Man of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Grand Old Man of India → Dadabhai Naoroji

  • Dadabhai Naoroji became one of the first Indians elected to the British House of Commons.
  • He was elected in 1892.

68. R.C. Dutt

  • Romesh Chunder Dutt was an important economic nationalist.
  • He analysed the impact of colonial land-revenue and economic policies.

69. Economic History of India

  • R.C. Dutt wrote major works on the economic history of British rule in India.
📌 Must-Memorise

R.C. Dutt → Economic Critique of Colonialism

  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale was one of the leading Moderates.
  • He favoured gradual constitutional reform.

  • Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905.
  • The partition came into effect on 16 October 1905.
📌 Must-Memorise

Partition of Bengal → 1905 → Lord Curzon

  • The government claimed administrative efficiency as the reason for partition.

  • Nationalists regarded partition as an attempt to weaken growing Bengali nationalism through division.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

83. Swadeshi Movement

  • The movement promoted:
  • Use of Indian goods.
  • Boycott of foreign goods.
  • National education.
  • Indigenous industries.

84. Boycott

  • Boycott focused especially on British manufactured goods.

85. Swadeshi

  • Swadeshi literally implied preference for one's own country's products.

Swadeshi → Indigenous Goods

86. National Education

  • Nationalist educational institutions were established to reduce dependence on government-controlled education.

  • Aurobindo Ghose.
  • Surendranath Banerjea.

96. Moderate–Extremist Differences

  • Moderates preferred:
  • Constitutional agitation.
  • Assertive nationalists preferred:

  • Passive resistance.

98. President at Surat

  • Rash Behari Ghosh was selected for the presidency.
  • The session broke down amid conflict before normal proceedings could be completed.

99. Cause of Surat Split

  • Differences concerned:
  • Leadership.
  • Methods.
  • Control of the Congress organisation.
  • Continuation of the Swadeshi-boycott programme.

100. Surat Clash

  • The session descended into open disorder between Moderate and Extremist supporters.
  • The two groups separated politically.

101. Effect of Surat Split

  • Moderates retained control of the Congress.
  • Assertive leaders were temporarily excluded from its organisational leadership.
